children: The data center industry could have significant room for further growth as AI drives demand for computing infrastructure, although power availability remains a key constraint.
David Auerbach of Hoya Capital said in an interview with Seeking Alpha's

, there was still a long runway for data center expansion, comparing the industry with a baseball game in which estimates ranged from the third or fourth inning to not yet reaching the top of the first.

The main constraint, however, was not constructing data center properties but securing enough electricity to operate them, Auerbach said. He described the availability of power as the major issue hanging over the sector as companies focus increasingly on the power equation.

as a major data center player with a large presence in Texas and said Dallas also has several private data center operators that could potentially go public in the following years. He also cited Prologis
, which has a data center business alongside its industrial real estate operations.
He also cited research from Link Logistics, a Blackstone

industrial spin-off, which estimated that each new gigawatt of power generation could support 2M square feet of additional industrial space. Auerbach suggested this could create a secondary demand opportunity for warehouses and other industrial properties as data center capacity expands.

title: Data centers have a long runway, but power is the constraint
